items.stem: Under IFRS 10's control model, an investor controls an investee only when it has all of which elements?

options.text: Power over the investee, exposure to variable returns, and the ability to use its power to affect those returns
options.rationale: Correct: all three elements of the control model must be present.

options.text: More than 50% of the voting shares in every case
options.rationale: A majority of votes is neither always necessary nor sufficient for control.

options.text: A seat on the board and nothing more
options.rationale: Board representation alone does not establish control.

options.text: A legal contract to purchase the investee within a year
options.rationale: A future purchase contract is not the control model.

items.explanation: Correct: all three elements of the control model must be present.

items.stem: Which TWO procedures are part of preparing consolidated financial statements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Eliminating intra-group balances, transactions and unrealised profits in full
options.rationale: Correct: full elimination of intra-group items is a core procedure.

options.text: Presenting non-controlling interests within equity, separately from the owners of the parent
options.rationale: Correct: NCI is presented within consolidated equity, shown separately.

options.text: Replacing the subsidiary's revenue with the dividends the parent received
options.rationale: Consolidation combines line items, it does not substitute dividends for revenue.

options.text: Measuring the subsidiary using the equity method
options.rationale: Subsidiaries are consolidated line by line, not equity-accounted.

items.explanation: Correct: full elimination of intra-group items is a core procedure.

items.stem: A parent holds 45% of an entity's voting rights, while the remaining 55% is held by thousands of dispersed shareholders who rarely vote together. Why might the parent still control the entity?

options.text: Its holding may be large enough relative to the dispersed holdings to give de facto control over the relevant activities
options.rationale: Correct: de facto control can exist where other holdings are widely dispersed.

options.text: Control is automatic for any holding above 40%
Control depends only on legal ownership of a majority of shares
options.rationale: Control turns on power over returns, which can exist below 50%.

options.text: A 45% holding can never give control
options.rationale: De facto control can arise below 50%.

items.explanation: Correct: de facto control can exist where other holdings are widely dispersed.
